audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows said the opposite of the why-text printed beside them, and the diff token says EVEN on a 49.08% lane whose tone colour, difficulty rating and final-rating line all say Hard.
audit.why: whys[3] ends 'trades are on his terms' but the row said Skill; whys[4] opens 'Blade of the Exile flips the script' but the row said Jayce; whys[5] says he keeps the HP lead but the row said Skill; whys[6] says 'a genuine coin flip on execution' but the row said Jayce. Every one of those flips moves the chart toward the packet as well.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 4, 5, 6 flipped as one atomic group across both layers (Jayce / Riven / Jayce / Skill) with ratings to match, and diff moved to HARD so it agrees with tone #ff5d6c, diffRating 8.5/10 and report[14].

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] tells the player Jayce's Sheen spike hurts 'through your Shieldbow' when the entry's own itemisation builds Eclipse into Sterak's Gage, and misspells Shock Blast as 'Shockblast'.
audit.why: The mitigation the player actually has at that timing is Valor's shield, not an item the page never told them to buy.
audit.corrected: whys[5] rebuilt on Valor's shield with the ability name spelled correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] and wants.foe[1] both credit the mid-combo knockback to To the Skies!, Jayce's hammer Q.
audit.why: Riot's text splits these cleanly: hammer Q (To the Skies!) LEAPS to an enemy and slows; hammer E (Thundering Blow) deals magic damage and KNOCKS THEM BACK. The ability that breaks a Riven Q3 is Thundering Blow, and the page's own spikes[3] already says 'bait the knockback (E)' — so the entry contradicts itself. A player watching for the leap animation is watching the wrong hand, and the knockback lands anyway.
audit.corrected: whys[2] and wants.foe[1] moved to Thundering Blow with its real 20-second rank-1 cooldown; To the Skies! kept as the leap-and-slow it is.
sources: enemyKit E text (Hammer: knocks them back)

audit.whatIsWrong: Shock Blast is the tracked cooldown across the whole entry with no number attached.
audit.why: It starts at 16 seconds and drops to 6 at max rank — the reason the lane is survivable early and unbearable later, and a fact that tells the player their early dodge window is real but shrinking.
audit.corrected: whys[3] now states 16s at rank 1 and that it ranks down fast.

edits.before: Your full Q-W-E kit is live but so is his entire cannon-hammer dual threat; he can poke you down through the Gate before you close distance, and To the Skies interrupts your Q3 if you close without baiting it first.
edits.after: Your full Q-W-E is live but so is his dual stance; he pokes through Acceleration Gate before you can close, and Thundering Blow knocks you out of Q3 on a 20s rank-1 cooldown — bait it on the approach.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 Jayce consolidates the poke lead into health bar control — he zones you off CS waves with Gate placement and you have no reliable way to approach without eating a punish, so trades are on his terms.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 he turns poke into health-bar control — Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 but ranks down fast, and Gate placement zones you off CS, so trades stay on his terms until you have Eclipse.

edits.before: Jayce's first item Sheen spike makes every hammer-stance trade hurt through your Shieldbow, and his ranged toolkit means he can keep the HP lead he built in the poke phase while you are still one Shockblast away from a bad all-in.
edits.after: His first-item Sheen spike makes every hammer trade hurt through Valor's shield, and his range keeps the HP lead he built in the poke phase while you are still one Shock Blast from a bad all-in he can punish.

edits.before: Use To the Skies (Q hammer) as a knockback insurance to interrupt your Q3 and create distance
edits.after: Use Thundering Blow (hammer E) to knock you back mid-chain — To the Skies! only leaps and slows

notes: Level 1 left as Jayce even though the packet says Skill: whys[0] argues in detail that a cannon-stance Jayce pokes a melee Riven for free at Level 1 with no answer, and I would rather keep the row agreeing with its reason than match a packet value the text contradicts. The mirror flagged the same packet-vs-page chart disagreement and chose not to flip it either, so both pages stay consistent. The knockback misattribution also survives in the 'mid' paragraph ('He will try To the Skies as a knockback mid-combo to break your Q3 animation') — that is the string the packet's suspectName flagged, and it needs the byte-exact pass; the same paragraph tells the player to 'back to complete Immortal Shieldbow' against an Eclipse build. Both are real, both are in long strings surrounded by mojibake em dashes in this brief, so I left them rather than risk a stale-before rejection. Jayce's Q and E are the only six-rank cooldowns in this whole champion set (they gain a rank from his R), which is why the rank-1 figure is the honest one to quote.
